linux-x86_64.scope: Structural/source/subject/input binding of one authenticated publisher bundle plus the externally collected protected signer-job success record. The caller must first authenticate the exact provider ZIP digest and complete member inventory. The recorded signer job ran the frozen source workflow; this readback does not rerun GitHub attestation or Cosign cryptography, and it does not show a consumer used this bundle. A consumer-verifier trace is required for consumed-provider evidence.

authentication_scope: Both protected signer bundles are source/subject/input bound to their own successful jobs. actual_native_lifecycle_commands.scope: One host's authenticated native lifecycle and original command prefix, published 0.1.0-2 to native 0.2 transition, migration, package removal and retained replay. The 14-command upgrade tail is label/order-bound here; detailed evidence is delegated to the separately required verify-native-upgrade-readback-a1.py. Interruption and matrix detail belong to their dedicated readback modules. This result does not authenticate the provider artifact or grant RC1 acceptance.

interruption_pair.scope: One archived actual-pair slice only. Caller authenticates transport/source; signatures, all other consumer observations, matrix, cross-host and RC1 acceptance remain separate.

native_upgrade_and_retained_replay.old_package_absence: coordinator assertion and observed retained/new command paths only; the artifact has no post-removal filesystem scan
scope_limitations: The result ZIP does not duplicate raw old host-authentication bytes; source-pinned hashes, observed authentication commands, and separately preserved authenticated input artifacts provide the provenance boundary.
The refused-build output directory emptiness and final old-package filesystem absence are coordinator assertions, not independently captured filesystem inventories.
This verifies readback coherence, not the provider signature, original source inputs, package publication, or complete RC1 acceptance.

metadata_reuse.current_canonical_matrix: Both hosts, two fresh roots per host, five variants, all 208 canonical artifact rows, with strict raw byte bindings.

metadata_reuse.scope: Historical runtime/memory data is eligible for exact-byte reuse only after the unchanged accepted code/input scope and current raw archive pins plus canonical native matrix match. No current or fresh AROS guest runtime is claimed.
